title: The Unified Shrinking Matter Framework (USMF) Version 3
abstract: USMF v3 is a purely geometric–quantum cosmology that explains the observed expansion history, supernova distances, baryon acoustic oscillations, and the cosmic microwave background without invoking a cosmological constant or new particle species. In this picture, cosmic redshift arises from a universal “shrinking” of local ruler scales (driven by quantum-geometry effects) rather than an external dark energy. An emergent clustering parameter Ω_eff provides the effective gravitating mass needed to form CMB acoustic peaks and large-scale structure. A flexible expansion law—combining a tunable power-law and an extra exponential term—naturally reproduces radiation-, matter-, and late-time–dominated eras and yields the correct sound horizon for BAO and CMB.
description:
USMF v3 builds on the idea that all rulers and clocks slowly shrink over cosmic time due to an underlying quantum-geometric connection. Key features:

1. **Generalized expansion law**:  
   $H(z)=H_A(1+z)^{p_α}[1 + k_{exp}(1+z)^{s_{exp}}]$, which at high redshift mimics radiation and matter scaling, and at low redshift produces apparent acceleration without Λ.

2. **Emergent clustering (Ω_eff)**:  
   A new parameter that behaves like pressureless matter in the CMB and structure formation, but is interpreted as an entanglement-network effect rather than dark particles.

3. **Realistic sound horizon**:  
   The baryon–photon sound speed integral $r_s=∫c/√{3[1+R(z)]}\,H(z)^{-1}dz$ is built directly into the model, matching Planck’s measured value without fine-tuned dark components.

Together, these elements allow USMF v3 to fit Type Ia supernovae, BAO distance ratios, and the Planck TT/TE/EE spectra at the same precision as ΛCDM—yet with no fundamental vacuum energy or exotic matter, only quantum-shrinking rulers and emergent geometry.
notes: USMF v3: Flexible expansion law and emergent clustering parameter included.
